title: GTA 6 on PC in Early 2027? What I'd Upgrade Now and What I'd Wait On
summary: GTA 6 PC is rumored for Q1 2027 but unconfirmed. Here's which PC upgrades make sense now, from GPU and CPU to RAM and SSD, and which to hold off on.
body_markdown:
Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19, 2026, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. That's the official list. The PC question got louder on October 13, 2026, when GamesBeat reported that Rockstar plans a PC release in the first quarter of 2027, citing four industry sources who asked not to be named. Rockstar didn't respond to the outlet's request for comment, and Take-Two hasn't announced anything.


So I'm not going to pretend I know what GTA 6 on PC will need. Nobody outside Rockstar does. What I can do is separate the upgrades that make sense regardless of the rumor from the ones I'd hold off on until there's a real spec sheet.


## Is GTA 6 Actually Coming to PC?


Probably, eventually. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick explained the console-first approach in May 2026: "Rockstar always starts on console because I think with regard to a release like that, you're judged by serving the core." At the company's shareholder meeting on September 17, 2026, he added that "the PC platform is becoming more and more important to our company over time." Neither statement names a date.


History helps a little. GTA V arrived on PS3 and Xbox 360 on September 17, 2013, and reached PC on April 14, 2015, about 19 months later. Red Dead Redemption 2 shortened that gap to roughly a year, from October 26, 2018, to November 5, 2019. A first-quarter 2027 PC launch would be much quicker than either of those gaps. Plausible, not confirmed.


## What Does Rockstar's Current PC Game Ask For?


The closest official reference is GTA V Enhanced on PC. Rockstar's recommended spec lists an RTX 3060 or RX 6600 XT with 8GB of video memory, 16GB of dual-channel RAM and a DirectStorage-compatible drive with 105GB free. Even the minimum spec says an SSD is required. I treat that as a floor. A brand-new game built for current consoles will almost certainly ask for more, but it tells you the direction: an SSD is now mandatory, and the recommended spec calls for dual-channel memory.


## Should I Buy a Graphics Card Now or Wait?


If your current card is still doing what you want in the games you actually play, waiting costs you nothing. I'd only move now if you're on an 8GB card and already lowering texture settings at 1440p. In that case, 16GB is the line I'd draw, because Tom's Hardware's RTX 5060 Ti 8GB versus 16GB testing found the 8GB card about 18 percent slower on average at 1440p ultra, and nearly 40 percent slower with ray tracing.


The two cards I'd look at first are the[GIGABYTE Eagle GeForce RTX 5070 Ti ICE](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814932769?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) and the[ASUS PRIME Radeon RX 9070 XT](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814126746?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) . Both carry 16GB on a 256-bit bus, and both list a 750W recommended power supply. The GIGABYTE card is 304mm long and 2.5 slots thick, so measure your case before you order. If your budget or case is tighter, the[MSI Shadow RTX 5060 Ti 16G 2X OC Plus](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814137977?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) keeps the 16GB of memory, needs a single 8-pin connector and a 600W recommended supply, and is only 227mm long. If a new card pushes you past what your current power supply was bought for, the[CORSAIR RM850x](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16817139333?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) (ATX 3.1, fully modular, Cybenetics Gold) leaves comfortable headroom over a 750W recommendation.


One more thing on timing. TrendForce expects conventional DRAM and NAND flash contract prices to rise again in the fourth quarter of 2026, by 10 to 15 percent and 15 to 20 percent quarter over quarter, and has warned that PC DRAM supply could decline in 2027 as more capacity shifts to servers. I wouldn't rush a purchase because of that, but I also wouldn't assume parts get easier to find by the time a PC version is announced.


## Is My CPU Going to Hold Me Back?


In dense open-world cities, the processor matters more than people expect, especially for frame-time consistency. If you're already on AM5, the[AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113877?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) is still the drop-in I'd pick for gaming: eight cores, 96MB of L3 cache and a 120W TDP. If you're on AM4 and don't want to replace the board and memory, the[Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16819113940?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) is the more interesting story. It keeps your DDR4, fits your existing socket after a BIOS check and gives you the same 96MB of L3 cache that made the original chip popular.


## Is 16GB of RAM Still Enough?


For most current games, often yes. For a PC you want to keep through 2027, I'd go to 32GB. On AM5, a two-stick kit like the[CORSAIR Vengeance 32GB DDR5-6000 CL30](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820982040?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) is the safe choice. Buy it as a matched pair. Adding a second, different kit to an existing pair is where memory headaches usually start.


## Do I Need a Faster SSD?


Capacity matters more to me than peak speed here. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 asks for 115GB at launch, and GTA V Enhanced needs 105GB. A 2TB PCIe 4.0 drive such as the[Team Group T-FORCE G50 2TB](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16820985144?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_gta-6-pc-2027-what-to-upgrade-now) , rated up to 5,000MB/s reads and 4,500MB/s writes, gives you room for a few big installs without juggling. Going to PCIe 5.0 won't change much in games.


## What I'd Actually Do


If you're on an 8GB card at 1440p, the GPU is the upgrade I'd make now, with a PSU if needed. If you're on 16GB of single-channel or mismatched memory, fix that next. Everything else, I'd leave alone until Rockstar publishes real PC requirements. A rumor is a reason to check your system, not a reason to rebuild it.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is GTA 6 coming out on PC?** Not officially. Rockstar's announced platforms for the November 19, 2026 launch are PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. On October 13, 2026, GamesBeat reported a PC release planned for the first quarter of 2027, citing four anonymous industry sources, and Rockstar did not respond to its request for comment.


**What are the GTA 6 PC system requirements?** There are none yet. The closest official reference is GTA V Enhanced on PC, which recommends an RTX 3060 or RX 6600 XT with 8GB of VRAM, 16GB of dual-channel RAM and a DirectStorage-compatible drive with 105GB free.


**Is 8GB of VRAM enough for a GTA 6 PC version?** No one can say until Rockstar publishes requirements. If you're upgrading now, I'd buy a 16GB card, because Tom's Hardware's RTX 5060 Ti testing found the 8GB model about 18 percent slower than the 16GB model at 1440p ultra.


**Should I wait for a PC announcement before upgrading?** If your PC handles the games you play, waiting costs nothing. If you're already planning an upgrade, TrendForce expects conventional DRAM and NAND flash contract prices to rise again in the fourth quarter of 2026, so waiting for an announcement isn't guaranteed to make parts cheaper or easier to find.


**How much storage will GTA 6 need?** Rockstar hasn't published an install size. Console pre-loading for digital pre-orders begins November 12, 2026. For reference, GTA V Enhanced on PC needs 105GB and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 asks for 115GB at launch, so a 2TB SSD is a sensible minimum for a gaming PC.
